decisions.decision: Construct Constraints using default and adjust budget in pack_exact fuzz target
decisions.rationale: Constraints was marked non-exhaustive, so constructing it from default prevents future field additions from breaking the fuzz target compilation.
decisions.quote: Built from its default and adjusted now, like the other four call sites.

decisions.decision: Add fuzz-build target to Makefile and include it in make ci
decisions.rationale: The fuzz directory is a separate workspace that cargo check from the root does not compile, allowing breakage to slip past local checks.
decisions.quote: fuzz-build: ## Compile the fuzz targets without running them

decisions.decision: Decline to run the fuzzers as part of fuzz-build or make ci
decisions.rationale: Running fuzz targets requires nightly Rust and takes a minute per target, whereas compiling them takes seconds.
decisions.quote: nightly and a minute per target, which is why that stays its own job.

decisions.decision: Do not pipe cargo check through tail in the fuzz-build recipe
decisions.rationale: Piping masks failures because the pipeline takes the exit code of tail rather than cargo check, returning zero even on build failure.
decisions.quote: Not piped through `tail`. A pipeline's exit status is the last command's, so

decisions.decision: Support overriding the binary path in verify-doc-output.py via SMYSL_BIN environment variable
decisions.rationale: Allows tests to point doc verification at the specific binary built for testing rather than an outdated debug build, which is necessary for mutation testing.

decisions.decision: Ignore the binary argument token when scanning for paths in verify-doc-output.py
decisions.rationale: When an absolute path is passed for the binary under test, treating token 0 as a path caused the script to skip all commands.

decisions.decision: Add doc_output integration test to verify manual transcripts during cargo test
decisions.rationale: Replaying documentation transcripts under cargo test makes coverage visible to mutation testing tools like cargo-mutants.
decisions.quote: The manual's transcripts, replayed against the binary, as something `cargo test` can see.

decisions.decision: Gate doc_output test to run only under the default feature matrix configuration
decisions.rationale: The documentation manual describes default-feature behavior, so compiling the test in other configurations would report false drift.

alternatives.reason: The pipeline returns the exit status of tail instead of cargo check, masking build errors.
alternatives.quote: the recipe piped cargo through `tail -5`, and a pipeline's exit status is the last command's, so it printed the error and returned 0.

alternatives.alternative: Replaying against the default target/debug/smysl binary
alternatives.reason: Mutation testing rebuilds the binary with changes, so checking a stale binary would falsely report mutants as caught.
alternatives.quote: rather than at whatever happens to be in target/debug.

alternatives.alternative: Skipping the test at runtime in non-default feature configurations
alternatives.reason: A test that passes silently because it cannot find its subject is worse than having no test compiled.
alternatives.quote: Compiled out rather than skipped at runtime, for the reason `global_flags.rs` gives: a test that silently passes because it could not find its subject is worse than one that is not there.

alternatives.alternative: Asserting only that the word MISMATCHED appeared in output
alternatives.reason: It allowed the test to pass even when zero transcripts were run and all commands were skipped.
alternatives.quote: The first version of this test asserted only that the word `MISMATCHED` appeared, which is satisfied by `ran 0, skipped 168, MISMATCHED 0` — a script that replayed nothing at all.

consequences.text: Future field additions to Constraints will not break compilation of the fuzz target.
consequences.quote: A field added later will not stop this fuzz target compiling, which is the point of the attribute.

consequences.text: Compiles fuzz targets during make ci so local checks detect build breaks.
consequences.quote: `make fuzz-build` compiles the fuzz targets without running them and is now part of `make ci`.
consequences.verification_quote: Verified by re-introducing the break and watching the gate fail

consequences.text: Avoids requiring nightly Rust and spending a minute per fuzz target during standard checks.
consequences.quote: Running the fuzzers needs nightly and a minute per target, which is why that stays its own job.

consequences.text: Fails the build with exit code 2 when errors occur instead of masking them via tail.
consequences.quote: Unpiped, it exits 2 with the break present and 0 without.
consequences.verification_quote: Unpiped, it exits 2 with the break present and 0 without.

consequences.text: Ensures mutation testing replays against the freshly compiled binary rather than a stale debug build.
consequences.quote: replaying against it exercises the mutated code.

consequences.text: Prevents absolute binary paths from matching input path filters and skipping all transcript commands.
consequences.quote: the absolute-path rule below would then match the program itself and skip every command in the book.

consequences.text: Makes manual documentation replay visible to mutation testing tools like cargo-mutants.
consequences.quote: The manual's transcripts, replayed against the binary, as something `cargo test` can see.

consequences.text: Prevents compiling features that would produce false drift against default-feature documentation outputs.
consequences.quote: a stale `--all-features` binary made a correct `SMY-W202` claim look like drift, because `exact-pack` was compiled in where the doc assumed it was not.

consequences.text: Prevents test from passing falsely if transcripts are skipped entirely.
consequences.quote: A gate that cannot tell "nothing was wrong" from "nothing was checked" is the failure this repository keeps rediscovering.
